tools.name: Antigravity
tools.description: Advanced agentic development platform with paired-programming agents, terminal sandboxes, multi-agent collaboration, and artifact canvas rendering.

tools.name: Cursor
tools.description: The most widely adopted AI-native editor. A fork of VS Code with instant codebase indexing, multi-file edits (Composer), and inline terminal error fixing.

tools.name: Google Jules
tools.description: Asynchronous GitHub agent that clones repositories in cloud sandboxes, navigates issues, runs test suites, and opens verified pull requests autonomously.

tools.name: Kiro
tools.description: Next-generation agentic IDE featuring real-time collaborative agents and multi-file intent parsing.

tools.name: PearAI
tools.description: Open-source alternative to Cursor built on VS Code with transparent model routing and customizable backends.

tools.name: Trae
tools.description: Adaptive AI-powered IDE by ByteDance featuring Claude 3.5 Sonnet / GPT-4o integration, workspace-wide context indexing, and agentic code transformation.

tools.name: Volt
tools.description: Open-source (MIT) agentic IDE built on the VS Code core that drives Claude Code and Codex agent CLIs over ACP and supports local LLMs via Ollama, with hunk-level review of agent edits and Git checkpoints.

tools.name: Windsurf
tools.description: Agentic IDE by Codeium featuring "Flows" that track real-time developer context and synchronized multi-step edits.

tools.name: Zed
tools.description: Lightning-fast, GPU-accelerated code editor written in Rust with deep model integration and multi-model assistant panels.

tools.name: Codeium
tools.description: Free AI code completion and chat extension for 40+ IDEs with low latency and enterprise self-hosting options.

tools.name: Continue.dev
tools.description: The leading open-source extension for VS Code and JetBrains; connects to cloud models or local models (Ollama, LM Studio).

tools.name: Supermaven
tools.description: Inline code completion engine featuring Babble architecture (acquired by Cursor; standalone product sunsetted).

tools.name: Tabby
tools.description: Self-hosted AI coding assistant server; an open-source, private alternative to GitHub Copilot.

tools.name: Aider
tools.description: Command-line AI pair programmer that parses your repository into a Tree-sitter map, edits multiple files, runs lint/test commands, and automatically commits atomic git diffs.

tools.name: Avante.nvim
tools.description: Neovim plugin designed to emulate Cursor AI's multi-file editing capabilities natively in Lua.

tools.name: Claude Code
tools.description: Agentic command-line tool capable of autonomous directory indexing, running bash commands, handling git diffs, and orchestrating complex multi-file refactors.

tools.name: Cline
tools.description: Autonomous coding agent extension for VS Code that executes terminal commands, inspects local browser previews, and requests human-in-the-loop permission.

tools.name: Codewhale
tools.description: Open-source (MIT) terminal coding agent written in Rust that supports any model and splits tasks across multiple agents.

tools.name: Codex CLI
tools.description: Command-line interface for OpenAI's coding models optimized for fast in-terminal code modifications and script execution.

tools.name: DeepSeek-Reasonix
tools.description: Open-source (MIT) coding agent for software engineering tasks.

tools.name: Flisk
tools.description: Agent-first local environment generator and CLI that automatically configures Docker Compose, Tilt, and Traefik stacks from an empty directory so coding agents can focus on application code.

tools.name: Gemini CLI
tools.description: Google's command-line agent utilizing 1M+ token context windows to ingest entire repositories for refactoring and debugging.

tools.name: Goose
tools.description: Open-source, extensible AI agent by Block that automates engineering tasks, script execution, and multi-tool workflows directly from the terminal.

tools.name: Imagera Code
tools.description: Paid terminal coding agent (CLI, built on OpenCode) that reads and edits a project, runs commands and tests, and works headless or through ACP and MCP; one plan covers Claude, GPT, Gemini and other models.

tools.name: jcode
tools.description: Open-source (MIT) Rust coding agent harness built for multi-agent development workflows.

tools.name: Kilo Code
tools.description: Open-source terminal-based developer coding assistant engineered for low latency workflows.

tools.name: Mentat
tools.description: Open-source AI tool capable of coordinating git workflows directly in the terminal (historical CLI archived; team pivoted to MentatBot).

tools.name: OMK
tools.description: Open-source multi-agent coding CLI for the terminal (TypeScript, MIT). Switch models mid-session; finish goals only when your test passes.

tools.name: OpenCode
tools.description: Provider-agnostic open-source terminal coding agent harness supporting custom agent loops, local model routing, and unified diff execution.

tools.name: Qwen Code
tools.description: Open-source AI coding agent CLI by QwenLM for terminal-based code editing, debugging, and repository workflows.

tools.name: Roo Code
tools.description: Community-driven autonomous coding assistant extension for VS Code (repository archived May 2026).

tools.name: RTK (Rust Token Killer)
tools.description: Single-binary Rust CLI proxy that reduces LLM token consumption on common developer commands with zero external dependencies.

tools.name: Xenon
tools.description: CLI coding agent that records every session event in an append-only hash chain verifiable on demand via `/evidence`, enforces deterministic hollow-answer checks, and exports manual verification checklists with multi-model and MCP client support.

tools.name: AgentsMesh
tools.description: Platform for scheduling and isolating multiple coding agents across distributed workstations.

tools.name: Althar
tools.description: Desktop ADE that turns requests into tasks, assigns coding agents, and has another model review the changes. Local models are supported through OpenCode.

tools.name: Bivy
tools.description: Workspace that runs Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi and other agent CLIs as sessions on your own Mac or Linux machines or a hosted cloud computer, steered from a browser or phone, with approvals and automations started by GitHub, CI or a schedule. Local models via Ollama, LM Studio or vLLM endpoints for Pi; MIT, self-hostable.

tools.name: Carbon Forge
tools.description: Hosted source control (a web service reached over MCP, no local model involved) where each coding agent works in a lane, a set of patches over the trunk, instead of a git worktree. A patch that no longer applies is reported as a named conflict rather than merged automatically, and git history is rendered from the record and pushed to GitHub.

tools.name: ccmanager
tools.description: Session manager for coordinating parallel CLI agent workflows across multiple repositories.

tools.name: Claude Squad
tools.description: Terminal manager for running multiple concurrent coding agent sessions across terminal tabs.

tools.name: cmux
tools.description: Ghostty-based macOS terminal designed with vertical workspaces and desktop notifications for agent fleets.

tools.name: Kodama
tools.description: Self-hosted API-first, multi-tenant software factory (Go CLI/server, Apache-2.0) running container pipelines and AI coding agents (Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Pi) on rootless Podman 5 or Kubernetes Jobs, with PostgreSQL RLS, NATS JetStream, REST/MCP edges, a model gateway for cloud and local OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible endpoints, gitolite-style Git access rules, and human-in-the-loop role inbox approvals.

tools.name: MulmoTerminal
tools.description: Browser-based terminal grid running parallel coding agent sessions with dedicated git worktrees per cell, backed by tmux.

tools.name: Orca
tools.description: Autonomous development environment built to orchestrate and execute a fleet of parallel coding agents.

tools.name: Orkas
tools.description: Local-first desktop AI workforce coordinating specialist agents and external coding CLIs (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode) with custom model endpoints.

tools.name: Paradev
tools.description: Open-source (MIT) parallel coding agent orchestrator for running multiple agents concurrently.

tools.name: ruflo
tools.description: Open-source (MIT) multi-agent swarm orchestration harness with adaptive memory, vector RAG, and native Claude Code / Codex integration.

tools.name: Sqwakie
tools.description: Live dashboard and peer-to-peer CLI/MCP messaging for Claude Code and Codex agents across a team's machines, with project kanbans agents can start, review, and finish. Free for 2 people; FSL-1.1-ALv2 (source-available).

tools.name: Valo
tools.description: Desktop workspace that runs Claude Code, Codex and local Ollama models side by side on Windows, macOS and Linux, with per-tool permissions. Closed source with a free plan.

tools.name: Vibe Kanban
tools.description: Kanban board dashboard to plan, dispatch, monitor, and review tasks across multiple agent CLIs.

tools.name: BrowserTools MCP
tools.category: Model Context Protocol (MCP) Servers for Coding
tools.description: Provides agents with headful/headless browser interaction, console error capture, and network inspection capabilities.

tools.name: call-me
tools.category: Model Context Protocol (MCP) Servers for Coding
tools.description: Hosted remote MCP server (Streamable HTTP, plus mobile companion app) that lets a coding agent ring your phone or text you for human-in-the-loop decisions.

tools.name: Chrome DevTools MCP
tools.category: Model Context Protocol (MCP) Servers for Coding
tools.description: Official Chrome DevTools MCP server enabling coding agents to inspect DOM, console logs, network requests, and browser state.

tools.name: Cloud Alter Ego
tools.category: Model Context Protocol (MCP) Servers for Coding
tools.description: Remote MCP connector that logs AI chat questions and shares rules and work history across Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, and other MCP clients, stored as plain files in your own cloud storage. Free / freemium.

tools.name: codebase-memory-mcp
tools.category: Model Context Protocol (MCP) Servers for Coding
tools.description: Local code intelligence MCP server connecting code, docs, and infrastructure in a persistent graph with change-aware test selection.

tools.name: Context7 MCP
tools.category: Model Context Protocol (MCP) Servers for Coding
tools.description: Dynamic context-curation server providing real-time AST symbol definitions and semantic codebase navigation.

tools.name: Docsy
tools.category: Model Context Protocol (MCP) Servers for Coding
tools.description: Read-only hosted MCP for library/version lookup and source-linked developer docs; requires OAuth account sign-in.

tools.name: Filesystem & Git MCP
tools.category: Model Context Protocol (MCP) Servers for Coding
tools.description: Official reference MCP server enabling agents to inspect git commits, staging areas, branches, and file structures securely.

tools.name: Geonode MCP Server
tools.category: Model Context Protocol (MCP) Servers for Coding
tools.description: Web search and content collection MCP server for documentation lookups and research; MIT-licensed server with limited keyless page extraction and a freemium API-key backend for JS rendering, crawls, and country targeting.

tools.name: GitHub MCP Server
tools.category: Model Context Protocol (MCP) Servers for Coding
tools.description: Integrates GitHub issues, pull requests, repository searches, and commit reviews directly into agent reasoning loops.

tools.name: Ironheights
tools.category: Model Context Protocol (MCP) Servers for Coding
tools.description: Local stdio MCP server and CLI (`npx -y ironheights mcp`) that lets Claude Code, Cursor or Codex check an agent skill or MCP config before installing it, returning an A–F grade with findings for prompt injection, credential reads and remote-exec installs. Rule-based and pre-1.0, so it misses many plain-language attacks. Apache-2.0.

tools.name: Kite (kite.new)
tools.category: Model Context Protocol (MCP) Servers for Coding
tools.description: Hosted remote MCP server (`https://kite.new/api/mcp`, plugin for Claude Code, Cursor and Codex) for an agent-first design tool: coding agents read and edit the same HTML/CSS design files, components, variants and variable modes that the team edits on the canvas. It is an MCP server, not a model, so local-LLM support depends on the client. Free plan / freemium.

tools.name: Oh My Android
tools.category: Model Context Protocol (MCP) Servers for Coding
tools.description: Native macOS app (MIT, free) that controls the Android Emulator and adb devices from a GUI; its built-in stdio MCP server (18 tools) lets Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or VS Code see and drive the emulator. It is an MCP server, not an AI tool itself, so local-LLM support depends on the client you pair it with.

tools.name: Postgres MCP
tools.category: Model Context Protocol (MCP) Servers for Coding
tools.description: Read-only schema inspector and query execution bridge enabling coding agents to validate database migrations and models.

tools.name: ReMCP
tools.category: Model Context Protocol (MCP) Servers for Coding
tools.description: Hosted OAuth MCP for terminal, file, and browser actions on explicitly paired computers; actions may change device state.

tools.name: Serena
tools.category: Model Context Protocol (MCP) Servers for Coding
tools.description: MCP toolkit for coding agents providing semantic symbol retrieval and code editing capabilities.

tools.name: sqlite-graph-memory
tools.category: Model Context Protocol (MCP) Servers for Coding
tools.description: Local stdio MCP server and CLI that lets Claude Code, Cursor or Codex recall from a markdown or Obsidian notes folder, combining vector search with hops along `[[wikilinks]]` in a single SQLite file; embeddings run locally via ONNX. MIT.

tools.name: Codestral
tools.description: Open-weight model specialized in code completion and fill-in-the-middle tasks with an 80-language vocabulary.

tools.name: DeepSeek-Coder-V2
tools.description: Mixture-of-Experts code language model with 128k context length supporting 338 programming languages.

tools.name: DeepSeek-V3 / DeepSeek-R1
tools.description: 671B Mixture-of-Experts (37B active) and reasoning foundation models matching proprietary models in code generation, multi-file reasoning, and complex refactors.

tools.name: Devstral Small 2 (24B)
tools.description: 24B open-weight coding model by Mistral featuring an extended 256k token context window optimized for repo reasoning and local execution.

tools.name: Llama-4 / CodeLlama Series
tools.description: Meta's open foundation architectures specialized for code generation, instruction following, and infilling tasks.

tools.name: Qwen2.5-Coder
tools.description: Open-source coding foundation model series (0.5B to 32B) for code generation, completion, and multi-file reasoning.

tools.name: Qwen3-Coder Preview
tools.description: Agentic coding model series (including 30B MoE and 480B MoE) pre-trained for tool calling and long-context code understanding.

tools.name: StarCoder 2
tools.description: Open, transparently trained code models (3B, 7B, 15B) curated by BigCode under permissive licenses.

tools.name: llama.cpp
tools.description: High-performance C/C++ inference engine for quantized GGUF models with minimal hardware overhead.

tools.name: LM Studio
tools.description: Graphical desktop application for running local GGUF models on Apple Silicon and NVIDIA GPUs.

tools.name: Ollama
tools.description: The easiest way to get up and running with local models via a single terminal command (`ollama run qwen2.5-coder`).

tools.name: Outlier
tools.description: Mac desktop app (Apple Silicon) that runs open-weight models such as Qwen locally, with a Pro coding agent that edits files and runs tests; free tier, Pro paid once.

tools.name: vLLM
tools.description: High-throughput, memory-efficient LLM serving engine featuring PagedAttention for production local deployments.

tools.name: agent-qa
tools.description: CLI and MCP agent for natural-language Web, Android and iOS testing, with persistent memory and validated self-improvement. Supports local models through OpenAI-compatible endpoints.

tools.name: code-review-graph
tools.description: Local-first code intelligence graph for MCP and CLI that builds a persistent codebase map so AI coding tools read only relevant context during reviews.

tools.name: CodeRabbit
tools.description: AI-driven pull request reviewer providing line-by-line feedback, sequence diagrams, and security vulnerability checks.

tools.name: Cover-Agent
tools.description: Open-source generative testing tool that iteratively generates unit tests until target coverage is met.

tools.name: Keploy
tools.description: Open-source zero-code test generator that captures real network calls and creates automated regression test suites.

tools.name: Qodo (CodiumAI)
tools.description: Comprehensive code integrity platform analyzing PRs, writing regression tests, and enforcing code standards.

tools.name: Semgrep Assistant
tools.description: Combines deterministic static analysis (AST rules) with LLM explanations to eliminate false-positive security findings.

tools.name: OpenHands
tools.description: Autonomous software development agent capable of writing code, browsing the web, and running dockerized execution sandboxes.

tools.name: SWE-agent
tools.description: Open-source agent developed by Princeton that resolves real GitHub issues on the SWE-bench benchmark using an Agent-Computer Interface (ACI).
